finding.claim: The POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban handler swallows the admin check's 403 and then performs the ban anyway, so any request whose g.user is a non-admin user can ban any uid. The unban route (lines 24-28) enforces the check correctly.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled HTTP POST to /admin/users/<uid>/ban. uid comes from the URL path (admin.py:15). Caller identity is g.user, which is populated outside this file; the repo has no before_request hook or decorator. Precondition: an authenticated non-admin user (g.user is a dict with is_admin falsy).
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the protected account-ban state change. Its body is a stub (`pass`, admin.py:31-32), so the present impact is the broken authorization decision, not an observable ban.

trace.note: uid taken from URL path with no validation
except Exception catches Forbidden (HTTPException subclasses Exception); it only logs a warning and does not re-raise or return
do_ban(uid) runs unconditionally after the swallowed 403
returns {ok: true} to the non-admin caller

finding.guards_checked: require_admin does raise on non-admin (admin.py:10-11), but the caller swallows it (admin.py:16-19). There is no decorator, before_request, or other auth guard in the repo. unban (admin.py:26-27) calls require_admin outside any try, so it is correctly guarded. Side note: if g.user is unset, line 19 `g.user.get` raises AttributeError outside any try, giving a 500 and no ban, so the bypass requires g.user to be set. Severity is high once do_ban is implemented; today it is a stub.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. require_admin (admin.py:9-11) does abort(403), but its exception is swallowed by the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18-19, which only logs and falls through to do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20. The repo contains only admin.py, so there is no before_request hook, decorator, or other auth guard. unban (admin.py:26) is correctly unguarded by any try block.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: require_admin aborts with 403 at admin.py:11, the `except Exception` at admin.py:18 swallows the werkzeug Forbidden, and do_ban(uid) still runs at admin.py:20, so any authenticated caller with a non-admin g.user reaches the ban decision. The impact is latent because do_ban is a `pass` stub at admin.py:31-32, and g.user is populated outside this repo, so the precondition is assumed rather than verified here.
